title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Paper ships a Remote MCP server (Nov 17): cloud agents can read and write Paper design files with no desktop install
bullets.summary: Paper (paper.design) announced a remote version of its MCP server so cloud-hosted agents can open and edit design files without the local Paper Desktop app; a companion PR adds a ChatGPT/Codex plugin for it. Launch details come from Paper's docs and an announcement relayed on X.
bullets.how: Brand 9 Signs: a cloud agent could draft sign mockups and proof layouts in a shared design file overnight without a Mac in the loop; worth a trial against our current Canva/Higgsfield path. The Construct: remote (no-install) MCP is the right shape for scheduled cloud runs. PRAGMA: a clean example of design tools becoming agent-callable.

bullets.title: Alibaba previews Qwen4-Max (Nov 16): agent-first coding and a 1M-token context window
bullets.summary: Alibaba opened a preview of Qwen4-Max, positioned for agentic coding with 1M-token context support, following the Qwen 4 lineup shown at Apsara. Benchmarks are vendor claims; no Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Mistral, xAI or DeepSeek model launched in the window.
bullets.how: The Construct: a possible low-cost second model for long-context batch jobs (log and document digestion), but test before trusting and mind data-residency questions. PRAGMA: another sign that 1M context is now standard, so clients should price on task cost, not context size. Brand 9 Signs: no.

bullets.title: Dreamteam launches an AI-native CRM with four agents and a 'Company Brain', backed by $53M (Nov 16)
bullets.summary: Former Freshworks executives launched Dreamteam with $53M across a seed (Together Fund) and Series A (Accel); it says 100+ paying customers in 13 countries use its agent-run CRM.
bullets.how: Brand 9 Signs: a watch item if our quote-to-reorder follow-up outgrows email and sheets. PRAGMA: proof that buyers will pay for 'CRM run by agents with a shared memory', the same pitch we make for operator setups. The Construct: the 'Company Brain' is our memory/knowledge-graph layer under another name.

bullets.title: Corma raises $125M Series A at $1B to train cybersecurity-tuned foundation models (Nov 16)
bullets.summary: Corma.ai, which builds AI models for security teams, raised $125M led by NEA with Khosla, Coatue and Sequoia returning.
bullets.how: PRAGMA only: security-specialist models are attracting big money, so client agent-security advice should expect domain models inside their security stack. No direct use for The Construct or Brand 9 Signs.

bullets.title: arXiv 2611.12545 'Teamknitt': configure, observe and step into teams of 1-16 LLM agents
bullets.summary: An open reference framework with 14 routing topologies (or custom graphs), shared-context profiles and human-led interventions; it states testable hypotheses but reports no comparative results yet (submitted Nov 9).
bullets.how: The Construct: a vocabulary for describing how our Hermes swarm routes work and where a human can step in; useful for writing down our topology, not for adopting the code yet. PRAGMA: a framework for explaining agent-team design to clients. Brand 9 Signs: no.

praxis_lesson: Prefer tools agents can reach from the cloud with no install: a remote MCP server keeps a scheduled loop working when the Mac is asleep, while a local-only tool quietly becomes a single point of failure.
